english: A coin is tossed once. If it shows a head, a die is rolled once; if it shows a tail, the coin is tossed two more times. Consider the events
$E_{1}$: the die shows an even number,
$E_{3}$: the coin is tossed exactly three times,
Then which of the following statements is TRUE?
(C) $E_{3}$ and $E_{4}$ are exhaustive but not mutually exclusive
hindi: एक सिक्का एक बार उछाला जाता है। यदि उस पर चित आता है, तो एक पासा एक बार फेंका जाता है; यदि पट आता है, तो सिक्के को दो बार और उछाला जाता है। निम्न घटनाओं पर विचार कीजिए
$E_{1}$: पासे पर सम संख्या आती है,
$E_{2}$: कम से कम दो पट आते हैं,
$E_{3}$: सिक्का ठीक तीन बार उछाला जाता है,
$E_{4}$: कम से कम एक चित आता है।
तब निम्न में से कौन-सा कथन सत्य है?
(C) $E_{3}$ तथा $E_{4}$ निःशेष हैं परन्तु परस्पर अपवर्जी नहीं हैं
solution: (C) $TTT\in E_{3}$, so $E_{3}\cup E_{4}=S$; $E_{3}\cap E_{4}=\{THH,THT,TTH\}\neq\phi$, so (C) is correct
solution_full: Sample space. A head is followed by one roll of the die, giving the outcomes $H1,H2,\dots,H6$. A tail is followed by two more tosses, giving $THH,THT,TTH,TTT$. Hence $S=\{H1,\dots,H6,THH,THT,TTH,TTT\}$ with $n(S)=10$ (the outcomes are not equally likely, but the question is only about the sets).

Events as subsets: $E_{1}=\{H2,H4,H6\}$. Tails can appear only on the tail branch: $THT$ and $TTH$ have two tails and $TTT$ has three, so $E_{2}=\{THT,TTH,TTT\}$. The coin is tossed three times exactly on the tail branch, so $E_{3}=\{THH,THT,TTH,TTT\}$. Every outcome except $TTT$ contains a head, so $E_{4}=S\setminus\{TTT\}$.
(A) Mutually exclusive means $E_{2}\cap E_{4}=\phi$. But $THT$ and $TTH$ lie in both, so (A) is wrong.
(B) Exhaustive means $E_{1}\cup E_{3}=S$. The outcomes $H1,H3,H5$ lie in neither, so (B) is wrong.

(C) The only outcome outside $E_{4}$ is $TTT$, and $TTT\in E_{3}$; hence $E_{3}\cup E_{4}=S$, so the events are exhaustive. Also $E_{3}\cap E_{4}=\{THH,THT,TTH\}\neq\phi$, so they are not mutually exclusive. Hence (C) is correct.
(D) $E_{2}\subset E_{3}$, so $E_{2}\cap E_{3}=E_{2}\neq\phi$; the three events are not pairwise mutually exclusive, so (D) is wrong.
originality_note: New: a two-branch experiment whose branches have different lengths, so 'at least two tails' and 'at least one head' are decided by the branch structure; the true statement needs the single outcome TTT to be placed in E3 (way 5: sample space construction linked with types of events). Closest known: NCERT exercises 'a coin is tossed; if head a die is thrown' with lists of mutually exclusive events. Different because: the events are chosen so that exhaustiveness of E3 and E4 hinges on one outcome of the tail branch and each wrong statement fails for a different reason.
blueprint_concepts: Random experiment, sample space and types of events

concept_use.Random experiment, sample space and type: The non-uniform two-branch sample space of 10 outcomes is built, and each statement is decided by checking mutual exclusiveness or exhaustiveness of the events as subsets of S.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, object and random experiment is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions, brute-force enumeration or sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan (Option C). Changed: No change.
key_step: Building the 10-point sample space and placing TTT in E3 but not in E4.
justification: Several statement checks on a self-built sample space; routine but each statement needs a genuine check. Level 2, similar in demand to the routine statement checking of 2021-P1-Q11 (L2).
